chapter: Nola band, day job and nightclub work
title: Blacksmith day job (and one night on the Capitol boat)
summary: From age seventeen he worked as a blacksmith with wagons and carriages until retirement; the trade was easier to find than music work and made playing hard. He also substituted once on the Capitol boat.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Did you ever play at the Capitol at Boat?

One time in my life, what time. I was called, just I'll tell you, shortage of people, I was called to take the place of a trumpet player. Well he wasn't in all the bands. No, no, no, I just called to do a job one night, one time. I see.
Who was on the boat then, what band?

Well, this fellow, the only one I can remember, a fellow called Faith Marble, who played the organophone. I think that's what you call that thing like a, played by Steve. The stereo. Yeah, yeah, he was playing. That was the only one I can remember. That was the only time I played on the Capitol. You said you had a day job with it. Yeah, well, you'll laugh at that. I was a blacksmith. Oh yeah? Doing wagon and carriage and cot days. I was a blacksmith. That was way back.
Oh yeah, that was way back. That was your first job?
Yeah, I was about seventeen years old and started to work at that.
How long did you stay on that?
Oh, I continued doing that until I retired now. I've been retired about fifteen years. Oh yeah?
Well, the business changed though, you know. They changed the automobiles and trucks and all. But it was similar, you know.
You still stayed in business? Eh?
You still stayed in business? Yeah, yeah. They kept it down.
Were there a lot of blacksmith shops in this neighborhood?

No, I never had too many. No. No. It wasn't too hard to get a job. If you knew how to work, that was what the people wanted. They didn't want that same thing about music. You want a good musician? You know, they want to hire somebody to try to get somebody who can do the work. That's the way it was in the back of the business. And I worked all the time. That's made it so hard for me, trying to play a music, trying to play a trumpet, and work too.
